title: Mathematical Modeling of Cellular Responses to Dose-Matched Stimulus Sequences: Weighted-Area Effects, Sensitivity, and Higher-Order Path Dependence
content: Cellular systems receive multiple signals over time, and the order in which those signals arrive can matter even when the total exposure to each signal is unchanged. This paper develops a mathematical framework for examining that possibility in a nonlinear two-stimulus model. The model tracks cumulative inflammatory and metabolic exposures together with an accumulated adaptive response. In cumulative-exposure coordinates, the response is a line integral along the protocol path. Green’s theorem then expresses the difference between two dose-matched protocols as a weighted area integral, with an explicit kernel determined by the model parameters and the cumulative exposures. For the two sequential orders, this gives a closed-form expression and a parameter-dependent reversal condition. The analysis is supplemented by local sensitivity calculations, a Monte Carlo perturbation experiment, and a variance-based global sensitivity analysis. A separate four-state control-affine example is used to examine the local role of Lie brackets and to show how higher-order path coordinates can distinguish protocols that agree in their total doses and in a lower-order mixed integral. The numerical examples use positive dimensionless parameter values; no experimental observations were fitted. The results describe mathematical properties of the specified models and are not measurements of cellular behaviour or clinical predictions.
